top_violation_types.title: Emergency Preparedness Plan - Evacuation, Relocation and Sheltering Procedures (26 TAC §747.5003(1))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: Emergency preparedness plan was unavailable to review

top_violation_types.title: Children's Records - Health Statement (26 TAC §747.603(a)(3))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: One child is missing a health statement.

top_violation_types.title: Written Operational Policies - Safe Sleep for Infants (26 TAC §747.501(6))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The operational policy did not include infant safe sleep.

top_violation_types.title: Fenced Outdoor Activity Space (26 TAC §747.4105)
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The provider did not have the fencing up around the outdoor play area.

top_violation_types.title: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Use Clear, Positive Statements (26 TAC §747.2703(4)(B))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: One of the caregivers stated to a schooler he was going to call the school to come and pick him up when the child misbehaved.

top_violation_types.title: Nutrition and Food Service - Drinking Water Available and Served (26 TAC §747.3101(f)(1))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The children were observed having morning outside time but did not have drinking water available to them while outside.

top_violation_types.title: Primary Caregiver in Licensed Home Qualifications - Proof of Training (A-J) (26 TAC §747.1107(7))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The Director was observed to not have 30 annual hours of training.

top_violation_types.title: Prohibited Punishments - No Harsh, Cruel or Unusual (26 TAC §747.2705)
top_violation_types.typical_finding: This was evaluated during a DFPS investigation and found to be deficient based on the sufficient evidence that caregivers restrained children in care by bear hugging them.
